summary:
Welcome to the Bad Beats Lounge, where Week 7 was less about close finishes and more about absolute demolition derbies. We had *zero* close games this week, folks. Not one. Just a parade of blowouts that would make even the most degenerate among us turn off the notifications and go outside. And when the closest margin is 21 points, you know it's been that kind of Sunday.

Let's start with our hero and villain. Cosmohouck is riding a three-week hot streak that has him averaging 147.5 points and looking like he's playing a completely different game than the rest of us mortals. Jonathan Taylor dropped 32.7, Trey McBride put up 24.4, and cosmohouck hung a 143.32-point beatdown on poor TophTT. That's a 92-point victory, people. That's not fantasy football—that's a war crime. Meanwhile, TophTT managed just 51.16 points with both George Kittle and Ja'Tavion Sanders combining for a cool zero. That's a Bad Beat if I've ever seen one. When your tight ends give you the same production as an empty roster spot, you're not having a great day at the office.

But let's talk about the real carnage here. Langland put up 50.32 points—and Spencer Rattler at 10.5 was the *star* of that lineup. When Spencer Rattler is your leading scorer, you've got problems that go beyond Week 7. Luke McCaffrey and AJ Barner combined for 1.4 points, and honestly, Langland should just forward his lineup decisions to me for next week's Bad Beats segment because they're clearly preordering content. And drobs? You started two quarterbacks—Bo Nix dropped 40 and Mahomes added 26.2—and *still* lost by 43 points because Jameson Williams gave you a goose egg. That's the kind of lineup construction that keeps me employed.

The mjgrana-powerperson matchup was the closest we got to drama, and even that was a 21-point margin. Christian McCaffrey and Ja'Marr Chase combined for 65.7 points, which is just unfair. That's like bringing a flamethrower to a water gun fight. Powerperson had DeVonta Smith go off for 28.8 and Jake Ferguson add 18.4, but when you're starting Kameron Johnson and Blake Corum for a combined 4.8 points, you're basically spotting your opponent a touchdown before kickoff. And mastab24 crushed Seananigans by 53.64 behind Quinshon Judkins' 26.4—which, by the way, is a name that sounds like it was generated by AI but plays like he was generated by the fantasy gods.

Here's the thing about Week 7: sometimes the fantasy football gods just decide that competitive balance is overrated. Six games, zero nail-biters, and enough blowouts to make you question why you check your score every five minutes on Sunday. But hey, that's why we love this ridiculous game—because next week, the guy who scored 50 points could drop 150, and the guy riding high could faceplant into oblivion. Until then, pour one out for TophTT, check your waiver wire, and remember: in fantasy football, it's not about how hard you fall—it's about how many people you can blame on the way down.
